On **October 14, 2001**, shortly after the September 11 attacks, federal authorities arrested two Iraqi nationals, **Zawahri al-Karbouli** and **Haider al-Karbouli** (sometimes spelled al-Karbouli/Al-Karbouli). They were charged with conspiring to aid **al-Qaeda** in planning attacks on the United States.

The FBI uncovered the plot through surveillance and investigations that revealed the brothers had been meeting with other terrorists and fundraisers in the Bowling Green area. Their goal was to procure materials (such as rocket-propelled grenades and explosives) and potentially travel to Afghanistan to fight with al-Qaeda, or to carry out attacks within the U.S. The case was significant because it was one of the early domestic investigations linking Iraqis to the global al-Qaeda network following 9/11. The evidence gathered during the investigation led to a lengthy federal trial, though the specific details of the trial's verdict varied regarding the extent of their direct involvement versus their support role.

So, to confirm: **Yes, the incident involved two Iraqi men being arrested for aiding al-Qaeda**, and it took place in the Bowling Green/Harlan County area.
